\section{Introduction}
Our reading of the parish registers draws on the 1911 cadastral survey,
whose parcel maps anchor the reconstruction presented below.
By linking each holding to its recorded cultivator we trace how
cropping patterns responded to the arrival of the railway in 1874
and to the sugar-beet boom of the 1880s.
The argument proceeds in three steps: we first reconstruct the
parcel geography, then estimate crop shares per holding, and finally
compare market access across soil classes.

\section{Background}
Cadastral mapping in the region proceeded in waves.
As background, the 1911 cadastral survey mapped only taxable parcels,
leaving commons and glebe land unrecorded; earlier waves from 1842
and 1878 covered the built-up core but omitted pasture.
These omissions matter for any reconstruction that aims at
complete coverage of the parish territory.
